sections.text:
Fix 8 verified bugs inflating the orphan/stale-block rate (node-only)
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/34

8 node-only fixes for verified defects that inflate the orphan/stale-block rate. No consensus or wire-format changes. Each is an atomic commit.

## Fixes

**Net / relay (low risk)**
- **per-peer rate cap**: count only *novel* blocks. The cap was sized 60x too low against the 10s block target, counted duplicates (incremented before the dedup check), and hard-disconnected honest peers at tip during fork races. Now: novel counted post-dedup at 60/min (10x the ~6/min honest rate), a *separate* duplicate budget that disconnects only a true replay flood, and soft-drop on novel over-cap instead of `TrafficQuotaExceeded`.
- **global rate cap**: never silently drop a tip-extending block (they bypass the cap — they are the scarce, time-critical case); raise 24 -> 120; warn-log on drop instead of a bare silent `return`.
- **stop silently dropping NewBlock/TipResponse** on a full event channel: warn + trigger GetBlocks/GetTip recovery (non-blocking; the reader is not stalled).
- **reorg trigger order-queue desync**: purge the order-queue entry on `take()` so stale ghosts no longer evict still-live reorg triggers under fork pressure; run the per-ancestor cap check before eviction.

**Miner / reorg (medium risk)**
- **miner torn-template lock order**: snapshot `utxo_set` before `tip` (same torn-read class as the prior PR #18 fix), and re-check tip equality before grinding.
- **self-mined redundant PoW**: connect freshly mined blocks via `process_block_pre_validated`, dropping a redundant Argon2id self-verify; log+halt on an unexpected local rejection.
- **reorg redundant PoW**: the reorg apply loop uses the skip-pow header validator for already-admitted fork blocks (integrity preserved by `get_block`'s `block_id == key` check + tx_root + difficulty); the trigger-retry path keeps full PoW.

**Reorg recovery (high risk, scoped)**
- **deep-fork re-admission live-lock**: admit a reorg-needed ancestor body past the fork-pool min-work eviction. A re-fetched ancestor was otherwise re-dropped forever for forks deeper than the pool, live-locking recovery. Bounded: it evicts the weakest *non-needed* entry, and the needed set is `<= MAX_GLOBAL_TRIGGERS (64) < MAX_FORK_BLOCKS (128)`, so a non-needed victim always exists — this is not a general bypass of the pool bound. Scoped to forks of depth `<= MAX_FORK_BLOCKS (128)`; deeper higher-work reorgs remain bounded by the pool (a pre-existing limit, and a >128-deep higher-work reorg is a 51%-class event).

## Tests & verification

**Regression tests added** (teeth-verified — each confirmed to FAIL on the pre-fix code and PASS on the fix):
- `reorg_trigger_take_purges_order_so_live_triggers_survive_cap_pressure` — order-queue desync
- `deep_fork_readmission::reorg_needed_block_is_admitted_when_pool_full` — live-lock fix
- `deep_fork_readmission::weak_unneeded_block_is_dropped_when_pool_full` — boundedness pin (the fix is not a general bypass)
